title: Choose the visual world for Ledgendary's marketing site
question: The roll assigned The Departures Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Departures Board
options.lineage: Mechanical split-flap boards in stations and airports
options.thesis: Every job an agency sells is a departure, and the board flips it from PROPOSED to PAID in front of you.
materials: split flaps with a hinge line
options.viewport: The whole viewport is one board: 'FROM PROPOSAL TO PAID' set in large flaps, live rows below each flipping a job through its stages, and the waitlist field as a flap slot that flips as you type.
options.risk: Transit is not an agency's own world, so it could read as a travel product unless every row is unmistakably money and clients.

raised.raise: Colour is a reserved signal: white carries text, amber only headers, green only paid, red only overdue.
No gradients, glow or shadows; depth comes only from each flap's hinge line.
Every departure has its counter-entry: an invoice flipping out pairs with a payment arriving.
Attention lights the board: rows at rest sit dimmed, the row that is moving is full brightness.
A closed set of six document glyphs (proposal, estimate, invoice, payment, expense, bill), used everywhere and nothing else.

options.label: The Duplicate Book
options.lineage: Carbonless triplicate order books: white, canary and pink copies
options.thesis: Write it once and it lands everywhere: the proposal, the invoice and the books are copies of one entry.
options.viewport: Three fanned sheets fill the viewport; the headline is typed on the white top copy and appears in carbon blue on the canary and pink copies beneath, labelled proposal, invoice and books.
options.risk: Paper bookkeeping is a familiar metaphor and can read old-fashioned; the copy colours turn twee if they are softened.

options.label: The Network Map
options.thesis: Every kind of work is a line, and every line ends at the same interchange: the books.
options.viewport: A map owns the right two-thirds: proposal, time, expense and payment lines converge on one interchange named THE BOOKS while a dot travels each; the waitlist is the 'Where to?' field.
options.case: Wins product clarity, because the map is the positioning drawn; ties on audience, since neither transit world is an agency's own.
options.risk: Flow diagrams are common in finance marketing, and a network shrinks badly on a phone unless one line is followed at a time.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The agency's books as numbered broadcast pages.
options.viewport: P100 index with jobs as numbered rows.
options.case: Loses both: a US agency audience does not know teletext, and pages of figures explain the path no better than the board.
options.kept: Reserved colour meanings, one per state.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.thesis: Every document a window on one desktop.
options.case: Loses both: nostalgia over money, and windows say nothing about one ledger.
options.kept: Depth from structure only, never from effects.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Debits and credits as forces holding the books upright.
options.viewport: A breathing column of balanced members.
options.case: Loses both: double entry as sculpture is clever for accountants and opaque to agency owners.
options.kept: Every figure shows the figure that balances it.

options.label: Collective Plate
options.thesis: One symbol set shared across every member's work.
options.viewport: Hovering document symbols on flat ground.
options.case: Loses both: decorative, and the money path disappears into the play.
options.kept: A closed glyph vocabulary used everywhere.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.viewport: Paths lighting ahead of the visitor.
options.case: Loses both: says nothing about money, and glow is the opposite of honest books.
options.kept: Focus lights what moves; the rest rests dim.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS landing page for agency finance, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and waitlist field on the left, a product dashboard floating on the right, feature cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every finance tool by design.
